statements.status_notes: No action required — finding is a false positive from Qualys passive UDP packet inspection against the underlying infrastructure/GCP load balancer; PingAM application code is not involved. Customers receiving this scan finding can be advised that Ping Identity and GCP engineering have confirmed no credible security risk and the CVE does not apply to PingAM (TRIAGE-27911, Resolved).

Ensure AM is on the latest maintenance release (which pins Ruby to a patched version per xxxx...). Confirm that the API Explorer feature is disabled in production (https://docs.pingidentity.com/pingam/8/am-rest/about-api-explorer.html). No further remediation action is required once on the latest maintenance build with API Explorer off.

No action required. The finding is a false positive confirmed by engineering (TRIAGE-32316, Jonathan Thomas, 2026-02-04). Ensure the API Explorer feature remains disabled in production (recommended default). No library upgrade or patch is needed for this CVE.

No action required for customers running PingAM 7.3.1 or later. If a scanner flags this on 7.4.x/7.5.x/8.0.x/8.1.x, reference TRIAGE-26934 and advise the customer to rescan against the latest maintenance release (e.g., 7.4.2) and treat any residual finding as a not-a-defect false positive per Ping's documented assessment.
No action required. The CVE was reviewed under TRIAGE-27239 for PingAM 7.4.0 and closed as Not A Defect. Customers running PingAM do not need to take any remediation steps for this CVE.

No action required. Customers whose security scanners (Sonatype IQ, NexusIQ, OWASP Dependency Check) flag xercesImpl:2.12.2 against CVE-2017-7503 should treat the finding as a false positive. The standard customer-facing response is: "This CVE relates to Red Hat JBoss EAP 7.0.5, which is not packaged or required by PingAM; the scan result is a false positive." Reference TRIAGE-26722 for the official engineering determination.

No action required. PingAM does not include pip as a runtime dependency. If pip appears in scanner output for a PingAM Docker image (e.g., as a wheel file in the base OS layer), it is a false positive — pip is only present at image-build time and is never executed by the AM process. Customers can suppress or document the finding using TRIAGE-27239 as evidence.
No action required. Customers can reference TRIAGE-27239 (resolved Not A Defect) when closing scanner findings: PingAM does not use PyYAML and is not affected by this vulnerability.

No action required. This is a scanner false positive against the Oracle Berkeley DB platform library. Customers should note TRIAGE-26934 resolution (Not A Defect) and reconfirm with their scanner vendor that PingAM does not bundle Oracle Berkeley DB. If on PingAM 7.4.0, upgrading to the latest maintenance release (7.4.2 or later) is still recommended as general hygiene, but it will not change the status of this specific CVE.

No action required. Ensure the PingAM API Explorer is disabled (default configuration). If customers are running an older maintenance release, upgrading to the latest AM 7.5.x or 8.x maintenance release is recommended as it includes an updated jruby version (xxxx...). Reference: TRIAGE-32316.

No action required for customers running PingAM 7.4.x, 7.5.x, 8.0.x, or 8.1.x — JATO was removed in 7.0.0. Customers still on AM 6.5.x or earlier must upgrade to AM 7.0 or later; as an interim measure they should apply Security Advisory 202104-01 patch (AM-sec-202104) and block /ccversion/* endpoints at the perimeter.

Upgrade to the fixed maintenance release for the deployed branch: 7.1.4+ if on 7.1.x, 7.2.2+ if on 7.2.x, 7.3.1+ if on 7.3.x, or 7.4.0+ (recommend 7.4.2 as latest maintenance) if on 7.4.x; also upgrade AM-SSOAdminTools to 5.1.3.28 or later if the admin tools are deployed. Customers on 7.4.0 who receive scanner alerts should upgrade to 7.4.2 and rescan per TRIAGE-26934 guidance.

Customers on 7.4.x should upgrade to PingAM 7.4.2 or later and rescan; customers on older branches (7.1.x, 7.2.x, 7.3.x) should apply the relevant sustaining maintenance release containing the xxxx... fix (7.1.4+). No workaround is available — library upgrade is required.

Customers on PingAM 7.0.x or 7.2.x should upgrade to at least 7.3.0 or the latest 7.4.x maintenance release (7.4.2+); customers on 7.1.x should ensure they are on 7.1.4 or later. Customers on 7.3.0+, 7.4.1+, 7.5.x, or 8.0.x should rescan — internal analysis confirms the fix is present and scan findings are false positives (reference TRIAGE-26934).

Customers on PingAM below 7.4.0 should upgrade to at least 7.4.2 (or the latest maintenance release of their sustaining branch) to obtain the Guava 32.0.1-jre fix; customers already on 7.4.0+ (including 7.5.x, 8.0.x, 8.1.x) should confirm they are on the latest maintenance release and rescan — no further action is required if the fix-inclusive build is deployed. Reference: xxxx..., TRIAGE-26934.

No action required for the CVE itself. Ensure the API Explorer remains disabled in production (default setting). If the API Explorer is enabled, consider upgrading to the latest AM maintenance release (which pins Ruby to a newer version per xxxx...) and keep the API Explorer disabled per Ping guidance at https://docs.pingidentity.com/pingam/8/am-rest/about-api-explorer.html

Upgrade to PingAM 7.4.x latest patch, 7.5.1+, or 8.0.0+ where the commons-compress dependency has been bumped to 1.24.0+ (1.26.0 in practice). Confirm the installed AM WAR contains commons-compress 1.24.0 or later (check xxxx... and xxxx... JARs). Fix tickets xxxx..., xxxx..., xxxx..., and xxxx... are all Resolved/Closed — no further action required beyond upgrading to a patched release.

No action required. TRIAGE-29726 was resolved as Not A Defect (2026-01-19) after engineering confirmed jline-2.14.6 is bundled inside jruby-stdlib and Amster but is not used in the vulnerable code path. No patch or upgrade is needed for this CVE.

No action required for PingAM. This is a False Positive in the product context per TRIAGE-33999 (Resolved 2026-04-28). Customers running container/IronBank images should note that the finding will appear in OS-level scans because there is no upstream OpenSSH patch for this disputed CVE; it can be accepted as a known false positive in PingAM scan results.

No action required for standard PingAM deployments. Customers running security scanners will see the finding against the nimbus-jose-jwt JAR (9.23 in older AM builds); Ping's guidance is that the PasswordBasedDecrypter code path is not used by AM, making this a false-positive finding in context. Customers who have concerns can confirm by verifying no PBKDF2-based JWE decryption is configured; upgrading to a PingAM maintenance release that ships a newer nimbus-jose-jwt build will also clear the scanner flag.

No action required. The scanner finding is a false positive — it detected xmlsec-2.3.0.jar in the AM distribution but the vulnerability is in Oracle's JDK, which PingAM does not invoke in the affected manner. Reference TRIAGE-32316 (Resolved) for the official determination.

Upgrade to PingAM 7.4.2 (or the latest maintenance release for your supported branch: 7.3.2+, 7.5.0+, 8.0.x/8.1.x which do not ship ion-java); re-scan after upgrade to confirm ion-java-1.0.2.jar is absent from WEB-INF/lib. No workaround is available for 7.4.0 other than upgrade.

Upgrade to the latest maintenance release of your PingAM branch: 7.4.x customers should apply the current sustaining patch (xxxx... fix train); 7.5.x customers should be on 7.5.1 or later; 8.x customers should be on 8.0.0 or later. No manual library replacement is required if on a patched release — the commons-compress upgrade to 1.26.0+ is bundled in those releases.

Upgrade to PingAM 7.4.2 or later (7.4.x line) or PingAM 7.5.1 or later (7.5.x line), which include the commons-compress upgrade to 1.26.0+. For 8.x, ensure the build includes the fix from xxxx... No manual library replacement is needed if on a patched release.

Customers on PingAM 7.4.0 should upgrade to 7.4.2 (or the latest available maintenance release) and rescan; no dedicated AM engineering fix ticket exists for this CVE, and the TRIAGE-26934 case was closed as Not A Defect after the customer's support case was closed without a residual finding

Customers on 7.4.x should upgrade to at least 7.4.1 (ideally 7.4.2 or latest); customers on 7.5.x should upgrade to at least 7.5.1; customers on 7.3.x should upgrade to 7.3.2; customers on 8.0.x should monitor xxxx... and apply the next maintenance release that resolves the ticket. Customers not using the SOAP STS feature have negligible exposure and can treat this as low urgency.

No official PingAM fix is available yet. Monitor xxxx... (master) and xxxx... (7.4.x/7.5.x) for resolution. Engineering has flagged the Spring upgrade as complex and blocked pending potential SOAP-STS removal. As an interim measure, assess whether SOAP-STS is deployed — if not, exposure is minimal. When a Spring upgrade (spring-context/spring-core >= 6.1.14 / 6.0.23 / 5.3.39+fix) is released via the openam backport stream, apply it. Customers should watch for a PingAM maintenance release that bumps the Spring dependency.

Monitor xxxx... and xxxx... for the spring-core upgrade backport (targeting a spring-core version beyond 5.3.39 per the CVE-2025-41249 companion work); no immediate emergency action is required since the Spring MVC attack vector is not reachable in PingAM's soap-sts-server. Customers should be advised this is a conditional/false-positive finding from scanners and await the next maintenance release containing the bundled spring-core upgrade for 7.4.x and 7.5.x.

No action required. The CVE is a scanner false positive — the OpenTelemetry exporter-sender-jdk JAR in PingAM is not the affected WordPress plugin. TRIAGE-29726 was closed as Not A Defect. Customers can cite this ticket as justification when responding to scanner findings.

No action required. TRIAGE-29726 was closed as Not A Defect on 2026-01-19. If a scanner flags this CVE against opentelemetry-exporter-sender-jdk, it is a false positive — document it as such in the scan report and suppress the finding.

No action required. The finding is a confirmed false positive (TRIAGE-32316, Resolved). Customers can close this finding in their scanner with the note: the scanner matched a Ruby stdlib abort-guard string inside jruby-stdlib; WEBrick gem is not installed or invoked in PingAM. If the API Explorer is enabled, disable it per Ping documentation as a general hardening step (https://docs.pingidentity.com/pingam/8/am-rest/about-api-explorer.html).

Customers on AM 7.3.x should upgrade to 7.3.2 or later; customers on 7.4.x should upgrade to 7.4.2 or later; customers on 7.5.x should upgrade to 7.5.1 or later; customers on 8.0.x should upgrade to 8.0.0 GA or later. No manual workaround or library patching is needed — the fix is bundled in each maintenance release. Customers who cannot upgrade immediately can reference Ping's official position that the vulnerability is not exploitable in PingAM because the affected XmlStreamReader class is not reachable via any PingAM code path.

No immediate customer action required for standard PingAM deployments — internal engineering has confirmed the vulnerable carousel component is not used OOTB. Customers whose security scanners flag Bootstrap 3.4.1 should be advised to treat this as a conditional finding (not an immediate exploitable risk) and note that TRIAGE-29479 / xxxx... / IAM-9281 track the Bootstrap upgrade; monitor those tickets for a fix release. Customers who have custom UI code using Bootstrap carousel (data-slide/data-slide-to) should mitigate by removing or sanitizing that usage until the Bootstrap upgrade ships.

No immediate action required — PingAM engineering has confirmed the affected Bootstrap button plugin component (data-loading-text) is not used in XUI or Platform UI; security teams flagging this should treat it as a false positive for current releases. Monitor IAM-7493 / IAM-9281 for the Bootstrap upgrade to v5, which will remediate the library-level finding. Customers on self-managed PingAM (7.4.x–8.1.x) who have customized the UI to use the Bootstrap button loading-text feature should remove that usage until Bootstrap is upgraded.

Upgrade to the PingAM release that includes the lodash-es 4.17.23 fix: 7.4.3+ for 7.4.x customers, or the next 7.5.x / 8.0.x / 8.1.0 maintenance release containing xxxx...–25706. No workaround is available; upgrade is the only remediation per engineering notes.

No action required from a security-risk perspective; the vulnerable cipher is unreachable in PingAM. Customers who must demonstrate a clean dependency scan for compliance purposes should await the next PingAM maintenance release that includes bcprov-jdk18on 1.84 (tracked in xxxx...).

No patched PingAM version is available yet. Track xxxx... (7.4.x/7.5.x) and xxxx... (8.1.x) / xxxx... (master/8.x) for fix releases. As interim mitigation, confirm that no AM UI customizations or themes inject user-controlled content into Bootstrap tooltip/popover attributes with data-html="true". Upgrade to the PingAM maintenance release that includes the Bootstrap 4.x upgrade once available.

Customers on 7.4.x should upgrade to PingAM 7.4.2 or later; customers on 7.3.x should upgrade to 7.3.3 or later; customers on 7.5.x should upgrade to 7.5.2 or later. Customers already on PingAM 8.0.0 or 8.1.x require no action. TRIAGE-26934 was closed after the customer was directed to upgrade to 7.4.2 and rescan.

No PingAM product upgrade required. Customers should: (1) verify their Tomcat deployment version and ensure it is not in the affected range (9.0.0.M1–9.0.98, 10.1.0-M1–10.1.34, 11.0.0-M1–11.0.2); (2) confirm that write privileges for the default servlet have not been enabled in their Tomcat configuration; (3) upgrade their external Tomcat runtime to 9.0.99, 10.1.35, or 11.0.3 as appropriate. ForgeOps deployments on platform 7.4+ using supported images from ForgeOps 2025.1 onwards receive regular image updates that include patched Tomcat versions.

No action required for customers running PingAM 7.5.2 or later with API Explorer disabled (recommended default). If scanner findings must be suppressed, confirm jruby-stdlib 9.4.13.0 or later is present (available in current 7.5.x and 8.x maintenance releases) and note the false positive rationale from TRIAGE-28566: the affected CGI classes are not invoked by PingAM. Customers on 7.4.x should verify their jruby-stdlib version and raise a support case if needed.

No action required. The CVE is a false positive for PingAM as the vulnerable code path is not reachable. If the API Explorer is enabled and scanner noise is a concern, upgrading to a PingAM maintenance release that bundles jruby-stdlib 9.4.13.0 or later will eliminate the scanner finding.

No action required. TRIAGE-27239 was closed as Not A Defect. Customers whose scanners flag this against a PingAM deployment should treat it as a false positive and suppress it with the TRIAGE-27239 reference.

(7.4.x sustaining) and sibling tickets — monitor those Jira issues for a patch release and upgrade to the fixed sustaining release once available. No workaround is available per the upstream advisory.

Customers who have not customized their AntiSamy policy file face no practical exploit risk even on unfixed versions, but upgrading is still recommended to eliminate scanner findings.

Customers on 8.0.x or 8.1.x require no action. If an immediate upgrade is not possible, customers can request the engineering-recommended exclusion of the spring-context transitive dependency from xxxx... as a workaround.

Upgrade to PingAM 7.3.3, 7.4.3, 7.5.2, 8.0.2, or 8.1.0 (whichever applies to your release train) to receive commons-beanutils 1.11.0; customers on 7.4.x who cannot upgrade immediately asked about manually replacing the ESAPI jar with 2.6.2.0 as a temporary workaround (see TRIAGE-28289), but the official remediation is upgrading to the patched PingAM maintenance release

Monitor xxxx... for a fixed PingAM release; upgrade to the PingAM maintenance release that includes commons-lang3 3.18.0 once available. Interim: no specific workaround is documented, but disabling or restricting any external input paths that could invoke ClassUtils.getClass() (e.g., custom scripts, webhook configs) reduces theoretical risk. No upgrade required. Customers can optionally remove ognl-3.2.10.jar from the AM installation directory post-install, following the same guidance used for other click-* dependencies documented in the PingAM 8 install guide. No service restart or configuration change is needed beyond the file removal.

Customers on PingAM 8.1.0 or idcloud-2026.3.0 and later already have the fix and no further action is required. Customers on 7.5.x or 8.0.x should monitor for the forthcoming maintenance releases containing the 7.5.x backport (xxxx...) and 8.0.x backport (xxxx...); given the non-exploitable client-side usage pattern, immediate emergency patching is not required but upgrading to the fixed release is recommended when available. Customers on 7.4.x should confirm backport availability with Ping support.

No immediate emergency action is required given the non-exploitable usage context confirmed by engineering (TRIAGE-31369, xxxx...).

No emergency action is required given the code is not reachable, but upgrading closes the scanner finding and removes the library-level risk entirely.

Upgrade to PingAM 7.4.3 or later (7.4.x customers), 7.5.3 or later (7.5.x customers), 8.0.2 or later (8.0.x customers), or 8.1.0 or later (8.1.x customers) to obtain bcpkix-jdk18on-1.79 which removes the vulnerability; reference xxxx... for patch details

When the next PingAM maintenance release ships with the Bouncy Castle 1.84 commons bump (xxxx...), the library-level finding will also be resolved. The jruby-stdlib embedded BC 1.79 copy will remain until JRuby upstream ships with BC >= 1.84.

Monitor TRIAGE-34987 for the official customer-facing response.

No immediate emergency action required for standard deployments; apply the next available PingAM maintenance release once xxxx... ships the netty upgrade. Monitor TRIAGE-34987 and xxxx... for release ETAs. If the AM instance is fronted by a reverse proxy that terminates HTTP/2 and passes traffic to Netty directly, treat as higher priority.

Upgrade to PingAM 8.1.0 to obtain the base image containing OpenSSH 10.3. For customers who cannot upgrade immediately, the risk is negligible provided admins do not use the container's scp binary to download files from untrusted sources with legacy -O mode; no PingAM product functionality invokes this code path. TRIAGE-33999 is resolved.

No immediate action required for runtime security — the vulnerable code path is not reachable in any supported PingAM configuration. Monitor xxxx... for the uuid upgrade to 14.0.0 and apply when a PingAM patch release is available. If customer scanners flag this CVE, reference xxxx... and the engineering non-exploitability rationale (uuid v4 only, no buffer argument).

Apply the next available PingAM maintenance release when it ships a JRuby upgrade that bundles net-imap >= 0.3.10; track xxxx... for fix availability. A full remediation requires JRuby 10.x which is blocked until PingAM mandates Java 21 minimum and asciidoctorj 4.0.0 is released — no confirmed ETA as of 2026-06-09.

No action required for runtime security. Customers whose scanners flag this finding can be advised that net-imap is a non-executed transitive dependency inside jruby-stdlib and is not reachable through any supported PingAM configuration. If the API Explorer feature is enabled, disable it in production as per Ping guidance. Monitor xxxx... for a future JRuby upgrade that includes net-imap 0.4.24+ if compliance policy requires library-level remediation.

No action required for security remediation. Customers whose scanners flag this CVE can be informed it is a false-positive scanner finding (transitive JRuby stdlib gem, no active IMAP usage in PingAM). A JRuby upgrade to address the net-imap family is tracked under xxxx... but has no committed release date; customers may apply that update when available to eliminate scanner noise.

No immediate action required; apply the next available PingAM maintenance update when released, which is expected to include a Netty bump to 4.1.133.Final or 4.2.13 resolving this and companion Netty CVEs. Monitor xxxx... and TRIAGE-34987 for ETA confirmation from the AM engineering team.

No immediate action required; the library is not exploitable in a standard AM deployment. Customers should apply the next available PingAM maintenance release when it includes the Netty bump to 4.1.133.Final or 4.2.13.Final (xxxx...). Monitor TRIAGE-34987 for ETA confirmation from the AM engineering team.

No immediate action required. Customers should apply the next available PingAM maintenance release once the Netty bump (xxxx...) ships. As a short-term workaround, disable Brotli, Zstd, and Snappy content-encoding support at the reverse proxy/load balancer layer if those encodings are not required.

(7.4.x backport); once a patched PingAM release shipping netty-handler >= 4.1.135.Final is available, upgrade immediately; in the interim, avoid relying on Netty IpSubnetFilterRule IPv6 subnet rules as the sole access control mechanism and layer firewall or OS-level IPv6 ACLs as a compensating control

No action required. PingAM ships sanitize-html@2.12.1 which predates the vulnerable code path. Confirm xxxx... is formally resolved/closed to reflect the engineering verdict already recorded in the ticket comments.

No fixed PingAM release is available yet. Track xxxx... for the netty-to-4.1.135 upgrade commit; once a patched AM release ships, upgrade to that version. In the interim, consider placing a TLS-terminating load balancer or WAF in front of AM to absorb oversized ClientHello messages and reduce direct Netty SniHandler exposure.

Customers on 7.4.x or 8.0.x should track the corresponding backport tickets.
